To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of corporate governance mechanisms by firms with high ownership concentration is associated with higher firm value.
concentrated ownership and corporate governance mechanisms are complements in Latin America.

(a) the use of a single corporate governance mechanism does not guarantee a higher firm value; (b) a combination of different mechanisms is more efficient than a single mechanism; and (c) the use of corporate governance mechanisms is not a substitute for the monitoring of institutional investors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the different mechanisms are used in Latin America and whether they substitute or complement each other.
the substitutability and complementariness of corporate governance mechanisms.
the following question: What is the role of corporate governance mechanisms for firms with concentrated ownership structures?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Latin American firms have been able to mitigate agency problems by implementing a variety of corporate governance mechanisms.
there is no single corporate governance system in Latin American countries.
the Latin American corporate governance system is a hybrid of the U.S. and the U.K. systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Latin American firms are not homogeneous and that there is a wide range of corporate governance mechanisms that firms use to mitigate the negative effects of high ownership concentration.
the more concentrated the ownership structure of a firm is, the more likely it will have a higher leverage, be cross-listed, have a smaller board, and have a dual CEO-chairman.
the more concentrated the ownership, the more important the role of the other mechanisms to ensure value maximization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effectiveness of these governance mechanisms is contingent on the degree of ownership concentration.
corporate governance mechanisms are substitutes and complementarities in Latin America.
Latin American firms rely heavily on the use of corporate governance mechanisms to compensate for concentrated ownership.
